questions.title: Explain XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) and how to prevent it in React.
questions.description:
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)

XSS is a security vulnerability where an attacker injects malicious client-side script code into a trusted website, which is then executed by the browser of an unsuspecting user.

Types of XSS

  • Reflected: Script comes from the current HTTP request.
  • Stored: Script is saved in a database and rendered to multiple users.
  • DOM-based: Script vulnerability exists purely in client-side code.

React's Built-in Protection

React automatically escapes all variable values rendered in JSX to text content, preventing HTML injection. However, vulnerabilities can still creep in.
questions.bestPractices:
• Avoid using dangerouslySetInnerHTML unless inputs are thoroughly sanitized using libraries like DOMPurify.
  • Never trust user inputs, specifically urls in <a href>, which can contain javascript:... links.
  • Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to restrict source domains for scripts.
questions.commonMistakes:
• Passing raw, unsanitized user inputs to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
  • Rendering user-defined URLs directly into link tags without validating the protocol.
questions.example:
// VULNERABLE to script injection via href
<a href={userInputUrl}>Visit website</a>

// SAFE URL Validation
const safeUrl = userInputUrl.startsWith('http://') || userInputUrl.startsWith('https://')
  ? userInputUrl
  : '#';

// SAFE HTML Rendering using DOMPurify
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: DOMPurify.sanitize(userHTML) }} />
questions.interviewTip: Explain how React protects by escaping string data in JSX, but showcase your security depth by detailing the href query protocol vulnerability and how DOMPurify sanitizes markup.
